elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1 retained sentence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of ..." and "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." No residual language leaves Customer uncapped.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered §21.1: "the greater of (a) the fees (including subscription fees) paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." The deterministic 'fees paid or payable' regex reports false only because the parenthetical "(including subscription fees)" sits between "fees" and "paid or payable"; in substance the basis is fees paid or payable, not the broader "all amounts", the lookback anchors on the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present. Lowercase "fees" plus "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" defeats the illusory §1.5/§1.6 USD 12,000 Implementation Fee basis.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.2 (untouched): "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations", and §21.1 caps liability "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is an Excluded Claim, carved out of the §21.1 cap.
§21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is listed as an Excluded Claim, outside the cap.
§21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims.
§21.3: "wilful misconduct" expressly listed among Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: §21.3 final sentence (retained): "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section."

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: §21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability" and "The cap is mutual".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: §21.1 as rendered measures limb (a) by fees paid or payable "in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" across this Agreement and all Order Forms, so the basis is genuine 12 months' fees rather than the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee.
§21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; §21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: §21.3 Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: with "Fees" defined at §1.5–1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and §21.1 further confined to the first Order Form, the pre-edit cap was far below six months' fees and effectively illusory — walk-away territory, notwithstanding otherwise strong mutuality and carve-out language.

The single operation rewrites only the cap measure in §21.1 and reaches the full preferred checklist: mutual cap, greater-of 12-months'-fees / USD 1,000,000, claim-anchored lookback, mutual indirect-damages exclusion (§21.2 untouched), all six preferred carve-out categories (§21.3 untouched), and the payment-obligations exclusion retained.

The failing deterministic check ('preferred cap uses fees paid or payable (not broader all amounts)') is a mechanical artefact of the parenthetical "(including subscription fees)" interrupting the phrase; the operative basis is still "fees ... paid or payable by Customer", not "all amounts paid or payable", so the element is met in substance.

Minimality holds: nothing outside the cap-measure sentence was touched, no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added, and the two clarifiers ("including subscription fees"; "under this Agreement and all Order Forms") are necessary to prevent the narrow §1.5 definition and first-Order-Form limiter from re-importing the illusory basis. Lowercase "fees" is deliberate and appropriate for the same reason.

Intent is preserved: the mutuality sentence, the mutual exclusion of indirect damages, the direct-damages characterisation of data-restoration and incident-response costs, and the Excluded Claims definition all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling (the narrow "Fees" definition remains operative for the payment provisions it was drafted for).
